description: I am Sheikh Samiur Rahman, a learner and love to keep track in goodness and truth
summary: This project demonstrates real space management and architecting of Martian and lunar outposts through real weather screening, real NASA heightmaps, challenge design and challenge-topic use, 40 parameters used based on time, energy, storage, heat, weather, day cycles, and radiation, decision simulation, and fun learning of scientific concepts. This project demonstrates learning of space and asset management guided by photos, videos, voice, and concepts given after missions. Our team tried its best to deliver well-structured and compelling tutorials at the beginning of the game, clearly articulating the challenge, the proposed solution and trade-off, and the importance of the mission summary through simulation. This proposed solution—learning with a delightful game environment and decision-asking within a challenge time—is scientifically sound and technically feasible, demonstrating strong alignment with established principles of science and NASA open data and API. The project demonstrates originality and innovation by our team members eventhough it was a two days hackathon, the team tried their best
details: This is a science-oriented space outpost management and building game. 3D model generation, animation, UI techs, API calls, and smooth programming through rapid troubleshooting were done. The concept pop-up played a crucial role in the teaching, and a mission summary was also provided at the end. Various brainwork models were analysed by us to decorate the challenges and scientific concepts. This game is exclusively better as it shows children how to explore games beyond just action/horror/parkour games or a regular dopamine dose. The best benefit of this game is that it increases calmer emotional regulation in the brain in tougher moments step by step. AI tools were ElevenLabs, Flow, Claude, and ChatGPT to accelerate the work. Little use of ComfyUI was also done. The programming language was C# and the programming software was Visual Studio. Blender and Higgsfield were used to generate the 3D models. The Unity game engine was used. The game will give students a love towards learning by happily playing with 3D models inside the computer that feel quite realistic in multiple languages. The project delivery was highly polished. It challenges conventional methods, presenting an original and inventive proposed solution that stands out in its field.
